title: Out-of-Area Replacement Reimbursement — How the Amount Is Figured
content:
The reimbursement of a covered tire replacement bought outside the Crestline network under Road Hazard Protection, where the damaged tire was not surrendered, is figured on the reimbursement date as follows.

1. **Out-of-area full-replacement period.** The period is judged on the reimbursement date: the replacement is in it while fewer than the plan's full-replacement months, as whole calendar months counted to the same day of the month, have passed from the effective date to the reimbursement date.
2. **Out-of-area coverage percentage.** 100 inside the out-of-area full-replacement period; outside it, the whole calendar months remaining from the reimbursement date to the expiration date, times 100, divided by the plan term in months, rounded down to a whole percent. Points added to the out-of-area coverage percentage apply only to a prorated percentage, and a prorated percentage with every point that applies is held between 0 and 100; an out-of-area coverage percentage of 100 stays 100.
3. **Out-of-area reimbursement base.** The lower of the out-of-area cap and Crestline's own price for the same tire. The out-of-area cap is the plan's out-of-area replacement cap, and Crestline's own price for the same tire is the covered set's unit price on its original tire ticket.
4. **Out-of-area reimbursement.** The out-of-area coverage percentage times the out-of-area reimbursement base, divided by 100, plus every allowance that applies to it; only that sum is rounded half up to the cent. It is paid to the tender the certificate was bought with.

The plan figures named — full-replacement months, plan term and out-of-area replacement cap — are those of the plan's schedules.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** A 36-month plan with a 12-month full-replacement period and a 150.00 replacement cap; reimbursement 14 whole months after the effective date, with 21 whole months left to expiration; covered set's unit price 139.99. The period has passed, so the percentage is 21 times 100 divided by 36, that is 58.33, rounded down to 58. The base is the lower of 150.00 and 139.99, that is 139.99. With no allowance, the reimbursement is 58 times 139.99 divided by 100, 81.1942, rounded to 81.19.

**Period boundary (hypothetical).** Effective date February 10, 12-month period: a reimbursement on February 9 of the next year (11 whole months passed) is inside the period; one on February 10 (12 whole months passed) is outside it.
